description: Semantic validity audit for referential instructions in Stage 18 eval set. Classifies whether each referential expression is objectively groundable from available scene inventory vs objectively ambiguous or unsupported.

referential_instructions.instruction_text: Place the nearer cube onto the farther cube.
referential_instructions.reason: cube1 at 0.40m vs cube2 at 0.60m from robot — near/far objectively distinguishable from robot_distance attribute

referential_instructions.instruction_text: Take the first cube you see and put it on the second one.
referential_instructions.reason: 'first cube you see' requires a visual scanning order convention (e.g. left-to-right, top-to-bottom) that is not defined in the scene inventory or system prompt. No objective grounding possible.

referential_instructions.instruction_text: Put the cube that is on the table onto the other cube.
referential_instructions.reason: Both cube1 and cube2 are on_table=True in the scene. 'the cube that is on the table' does not uniquely identify one cube. The reference is objectively ambiguous given available predicates.

referential_instructions.instruction_text: Put the one that is closer to the edge onto the other one.
referential_instructions.reason: Both cubes are in Center region with near_edges=[]. Neither is closer to any table edge within the 0.10m edge_threshold. The reference is objectively ungroundable from available edge proximity data.

referential_instructions.instruction_text: Stack the block that is on the table on top of the other block.
referential_instructions.reason: Same as ref_003 — both blocks are on_table=True. 'the block that is on the table' does not uniquely identify one cube.

referential_instructions.instruction_text: Move the block closer to you onto the one further away.
referential_instructions.reason: cube1 is closer to robot (front direction). Robot-relative distance objectively distinguishes the two cubes.

referential_instructions.instruction_text: Put the cube that is farther from the robot onto the nearer one.
referential_instructions.reason: cube2 is farther from robot. robot_distance values (0.60m vs 0.40m) objectively distinguish the two cubes.

referential_instructions.instruction_text: Pick up the cube that is not green and put it on the green cube.
referential_instructions.reason: Color negation: only red and green cubes exist. 'not green' uniquely identifies cube1 (red).

referential_instructions.instruction_text: 把离你近的方块放到离你远的方块上。
referential_instructions.reason: Chinese equivalent of 'nearer to farther'. robot_distance objectively distinguishes the two cubes.

referential_instructions.instruction_text: 离机器人最近的那个方块放到最远的方块上。
referential_instructions.reason: Chinese 'closest to robot to farthest'. robot_distance objectively distinguishes the two cubes.

referential_instructions.instruction_text: Put the lighter colored cube on the darker one.
referential_instructions.reason: 'lighter/darker' requires luminance/brightness comparison. Scene inventory only provides color names (red, green) without brightness metrics. No objective ground truth for which is 'lighter'.

referential_instructions.instruction_text: Place the bright cube on the dull cube.
referential_instructions.reason: 'bright/dull' requires brightness perception beyond available color labels. No brightness annotation in scene inventory.

semantic_validity_definitions.objectively_groundable: The referential expression can be uniquely resolved from available scene predicates (position, color, robot_distance, on_table, near_edges, spatial relations). A competent model should produce the correct binding.
semantic_validity_definitions.objectively_ambiguous: The expression refers to a property shared equally by multiple objects in the scene (e.g. both cubes are on_table, both are in Center). No model can resolve it correctly because the ground-truth binding is arbitrary given available data. Ungroundable is the correct output.
semantic_validity_definitions.unsupported_reference_frame: The expression requires a frame of reference, convention, or sensor modality not present in the scene inventory (e.g. 'first cube you see' needs a visual scanning order, 'lighter/darker' needs luminance). Ungroundable is the correct output.
semantic_validity_definitions.requires_missing_predicate: The expression would be groundable if a specific predicate were added to the scene inventory, but that predicate is not currently computed.
semantic_validity_definitions.evaluator_mismatch: The evaluator expected a binding that does not match what the scene data supports. The original ground-truth label may be incorrect for this instruction under the current scene.

reference_type_definitions.robot_relative_near_far: nearer/farther/closer to robot/further from robot — resolved via robot_distance attribute
reference_type_definitions.table_edge: closer to edge/at the edge — resolved via near_edges attribute
reference_type_definitions.on_table: on the table/on the surface — resolved via on_table attribute
reference_type_definitions.visual_order: first/second you see — requires visual scanning convention
reference_type_definitions.other_object: negation or exclusion (e.g. 'not green') — resolved via color attribute
reference_type_definitions.color_attribute: lighter/darker/bright/dull — requires brightness metric beyond color name
